questions.prompt: What is the mode of a dataset?
options: The value that appears most often
The total divided by the count
questions.explanation: The mode is simply the most frequent value.
questions.misconception: The middle value is the median and total ÷ count is the mean — the mode only needs counting.

questions.explanation: Count appearances: 4 appears three times — more than any other value.
questions.misconception: The mode is about repetition, not the middle (median) or position — 4 simply shows up most.

questions.prompt: If two values both appear 5 times and everything else fewer, the dataset has...
questions.explanation: A tie at the top gives two modes — a bimodal set.
questions.misconception: The tie does not cancel the modes — both top counters win, giving two modes.

questions.prompt: When does a dataset have NO mode?
options: When every value appears equally often
questions.explanation: With all values tied in frequency there is no single winner — no mode.
questions.misconception: Equal frequencies remove the winner; sorting or how many numbers there are don't.

questions.prompt: Why is the mode special among mean, median, and mode?
options: It works for colors and words, not just numbers
It ignores the most common value
questions.explanation: Counting categories works the same as counting numbers — the mode handles non-numeric data.
questions.misconception: Mean and median need numbers; the mode only counts, so it handles categories like colors and words.
